concerns.text: FR-006 specifies a Two One‑Sided Tests (TOST) equivalence test with a 15 % margin, power ≥ 0.80 and effect size d = 0.5, but the original idea only called for a paired‑t test and gave no justification for these parameters. This adds a new statistical framework not requested by the idea, constituting over‑reach and a potential drift in the research question.

FR-008 requires validation of the PyBullet filter against an independent physics engine (MuJoCo) to ensure non‑circular correlation. The idea never mentioned such a validation step, so this requirement is beyond the scope of the original proposal.

FR-009 mandates physics‑preserving data augmentation when the curated set falls below 30 samples. The idea did not include any augmentation strategy; introducing it changes the data generation pipeline and may affect the independence assumptions of the planned statistical test.

FR-007 calls for a concrete CPU‑only audit task (e.g., a script asserting `torch.cuda.is_available() is False`). The idea only required that the system run on a CPU‑only environment but did not specify an explicit audit, making this an unrequested feature.
SC-005 adds a training‑time limit (≤ 6 h on a free‑tier GitHub Actions runner). The original idea never set a runtime budget, so this success criterion extends the scope beyond what was proposed.

SC-006 requires computing a Pearson/Spearman correlation < 0.95 between the PyBullet filter and a MuJoCo validator. This analysis was not part of the idea and introduces an additional validation metric not originally requested.
